q_45367.question_text: What will be NVIDIA's forward guidance in its Q2 FY2027 earnings release? (Revenue)
q_45367.reasoning:
# NVIDIA Q2 FY2027 Forward Guidance Analysis

## (a) Time left until resolution
The question asks about NVIDIA's forward guidance to be issued in their Q2 FY2027 earnings release. Based on the research provided, today is August 24, 2026. The research mentions Q2 FY2027 earnings preview dated August 26, 2026, suggesting the earnings release is imminent (likely within 2 days). Resolution will occur when NVIDIA issues its forward guidance for Q3 FY2027 (the next quarter) during this earnings call.

## (b) Most likely outcome and why

NVIDIA has already provided forward guidance for Q2 FY2027 on May 20, 2026: **$91.0 billion ± 2%** (range: $89.2 billion to $92.8 billion).

The question asks what guidance will be issued at the Q2 FY2027 earnings release. This guidance, when released in late August 2026, will be for Q3 FY2027 (the subsequent quarter), not a restatement of Q2 guidance.

However, the research data strongly anchors expectations:
- Q1 FY2027 actual revenue: $81.6 billion
- Q2 FY2027 guidance midpoint: $91.0 billion (11.5% sequential growth)
- Wall Street consensus for Q2 FY2027: $91.9 billion
- Year-over-year growth from Q2 FY2026: from $46.7B to ~$91B (95% YoY growth)

The forward guidance issued at earnings will likely be for Q3 FY2027. Based on:
1. Strong momentum (Q1→Q2 growing 11.5%)
2. Continued data center demand despite China restrictions
3. Wall Street consensus slightly above the midpoint
4. The company has maintained consistent forward guidance execution

The most likely outcome is that NVIDIA will guide Q3 FY2027 slightly above Q2 at approximately $96-100 billion, representing 5-10% sequential growth (slightly decelerating from Q1→Q2 but still robust).

## (c) What would push the value lower?

- Macroeconomic deterioration affecting AI capex spending by cloud providers
- Unexpected supply chain constraints
- Loss of major customer or demand softening from hyperscalers
- Geopolitical escalation affecting export licensing beyond current China restrictions
- Competitive pressure from AMD or other alternatives materializing faster than expected
- Market saturation in AI infrastructure deployments

## (d) What would push the value higher?

- Acceleration of AI adoption across new verticals and regions
- Surprise demand from enterprise or non-cloud segments
- Resolution of China restrictions or policy changes allowing incremental revenue
- Data center buildout accelerating beyond current expectations
- New product announcements driving upgrade cycles
- Continued strong hyperscaler capex exceeding current guidance

## (e) Base rate or historical reference values

The research provides:
- Q1 FY2027: $81.6 billion
- Q2 FY2027 guidance: $91.0 billion (midpoint) with 11.5% sequential growth
- Q2 FY2026 (year ago): $46.7 billion
- Wall Street consensus: $91.9 billion

NVIDIA's recent track record shows guidance that is typically conservative to slightly beat. The company has guided within a ±2% range for Q2. Sequential growth rates of 5-15% have been common in recent quarters for NVIDIA given the AI data center supercycle.

---

## Probability Distribution Reasoning

The guidance range provided ($99.5B to $115.5B) appears to be for Q3 FY2027 (the forward guidance to be issued, not Q2 itself). 

Given:
- Q2 FY2027 guidance: $91.0B (midpoint)
- Q2→Q3 historical growth patterns: typically 5-15% sequential
- Current momentum and market conditions
- The provided range center (~$107.5B) implies ~18% sequential growth Q2→Q3

An 18% sequential growth would represent acceleration from the 11.5% Q1→Q2 growth, which is plausible but on the optimistic side given:
- Potential deceleration curve as the supercycle matures
- Tough comps building
- Current guidance conservatism

My estimate: Q3 FY2027 forward guidance will likely be in the $95-105B range (5-15% sequential growth), with a modal estimate around $98-100B.

q_45367.research_text:
NVIDIA's forward guidance for Q2 FY2027 revenue, issued on May 20, 2026, is \$91.0 billion, plus or minus 2% [investor.nvidia.com](https://investor.nvidia.com/news/press-release-details/2026/NVIDIA-Announces-Financial-Results-for-First-Quarter-Fiscal-2027/). This range implies a ceiling near \$92.8 billion and a floor near \$89.2 billion [fool.com](https://www.fool.com/investing/2026/08/19/nvidia-guided-to-usd91-billion-wall-street-penciled-in-usd92-billion/).

This guidance assumes no Data Center compute revenue from China, a stance the company has maintained since April 2025 due to U.S. licensing requirements for H20 chips [fool.com](https://www.fool.com/investing/2026/08/19/nvidia-guided-to-usd91-billion-wall-street-penciled-in-usd92-billion/). Wall Street analysts' average estimate for Q2 FY2027 revenue is around \$91.9 billion [fool.com](https://www.fool.com/investing/2026/08/19/nvidia-guided-to-usd91-billion-wall-street-penciled-in-usd92-billion/), which falls within NVIDIA's provided range. For comparison, Q1 FY2027 revenue was \$81.6 billion [investor.nvidia.com](https://investor.nvidia.com/news/press-release-details/2026/NVIDIA-Announces-Financial-Results-for-First-Quarter-Fiscal-2027/), and the year-ago Q2 FY2026 revenue was \$46.7 billion [ecmsource.com](https://ecmsource.com/nvidia-nvda-q2-fy27-earnings-preview-august-26-2026/).
